precepts.point: We read this all the time, but you don't understand what Noah dealt with. There's babies out there. People: please, my baby, please. Screaming and crying. His family out there too; Noah had siblings, sons and daughters out there screaming: why are you doing this? Noah had to sit there and take it, hear the screaming, the crying, the begging, until you hear nothing no more. That's a terrible thing to experience, man.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Noah was found righteous “in this generation” because he kept the commandments; that is how he knew the clean beasts from the unclean and how he walked with God. When the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened, only the eight souls on that boat lived.

It is the same today. Right now the door of repentance is open, and Christ is longsuffering with our people. This is the time to get it right. Once that door is closed, that is it; no one can open it, the way the great gulf is fixed. As it was in the days of Noah, so it is now.

precepts.text: Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet. That is the bowing down.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the kings and queens of the nations “shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet.” Christ says the same thing in Revelation: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet.”

Those that say they are Jews and are not, but do lie, will be made to come and worship before the feet of the true Israel. That is the bowing down. Before thy feet in Revelation is with their face toward the earth, licking up the dust of thy feet, in Isaiah. The two scriptures say the same thing.

We can hardly fathom these words right now. Who is going to bow down in front of the black man? People will look at it and say you are dreaming. But guess what? That is what the scripture says. Let God be true, and every man a liar.

So don’t worry about the hatred, and don’t worry about what we are going through here. Christ is coming to save us from the hand of all that hate us, and what we have coming is greater: the Lord lifts up his hand to the Gentiles, they bring Israel’s sons in their arms and carry her daughters upon their shoulders, and “thou shalt know that I am the Lord: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.”

Revelation 2:9 names the blasphemy: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” They are the chief house of the devil; they are Satan, the one the dragon gave his seat, his power and his authority.

Revelation 3:9: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews”, the Israelis, “and are not, but do lie”: they lie, they blaspheme about being Jews. “Behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.” They will know who the real Jews are, because it is obviously not them.

Their own history shows it. The encyclopedia records that King Bulan reigned over the Khazars, in what is modern-day Ukraine, and after questioning a Muslim, a Christian and a Jew he adopted Judaism. These were Europeans who converted to Judaism, and the Khazars became the Israelis of today. Hasdai’s letter even preserves the tradition that the Khazars once dwelt near the Seir mountains. They say they are Jews, and are not.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Philadelphia means brotherly love, and that church was a colony of Israelites. Christ, “he that hath the key of David”, tells them: “behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it”. That open door is salvation. “For thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.” They were under persecution, so he says he will make the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet.

Then verse 10: “Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world”. The hour of temptation is Jacob’s trouble, which leads into the world war and Armageddon. The church of Philadelphia will not be there when it happens. Does that mean a force field around them? No. They are at rest.

Isaiah 57 shows it: “The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” That is exactly what we just read in Revelation 3:10. “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.” Each one walking: they are not dead.

So when brothers and sisters die and people say, they keep dying, listen: I have a reason. They are at rest. You do your little tears and cry, that’s fine, but the Lord is keeping the righteous from the evil to come, the way he kept Philadelphia from the hour of temptation.

precepts.text: The unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God; and such were some of you.
precepts.point: To him that overcometh will Christ grant to sit with him in his throne. Rank or no rank, a brother must stay the same trooper.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame”. That is the business we are in: we have to overcome. With rank or without rank, a brother has to stay the same trooper. Don’t bail out now; it is time to stand up and face what we have to face.

What we have to overcome, Paul lays out: “Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” Your mother, your father, your aunt, if they are living an unrighteous life, will not inherit the kingdom. “Be not deceived”: not by Christianity, not by religion, not by the white man, not by the uncle or auntie telling you that you are in a cult. Satan can deceive you into leaving this life while you think you are still in the faith.

“Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind”. A lot of us are fighting the fornication spirit, the covetous spirit, the lustful demons. “Nor thieves”: some cannot stop stealing even in this truth, like the brother who borrowed the book and never brought it back. “Nor drunkards”: know your limit, because the drink spirit brings out whatever defilement is in your mind.

“And such were some of you.” That is the life we came from, so don’t think Satan won’t tempt you with these things now. And Galatians 6 warns: “if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work”. It is by the grace of God that you stand. When a brother or sister gets knocked out in this truth, your job is to fast and pray, never to applaud. Be your brother’s keeper; your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his. That is how we overcome.

That is a call for all of us to examine ourselves. Cast away every burden and sin, and follow the Most High and his son fully, keeping the commandments. The lukewarm who know the truth but keep no commandments will be cast away. Being spewed out of Christ’s mouth is the end of the middle ground, and the next step after that is death.
